dossier.orientation: This is a website analytics tool that counts pageviews without cookies, trackers or a consent prompt, which this buyer can install to run alongside their existing GA4 setup and see how many pageviews GA4 is missing once visitors decline cookie consent.

setup_conditions: Install Simple Analytics to run alongside the existing GA4 tracking, with vendor-assisted setup covering proxies and custom domains where needed, as part of the 30-day comparison offer.
unverified_requirements: Whether the measured pageview gap can be isolated as caused specifically by consent rejection, as opposed to blocking or general implementation differences, which Simple Analytics' own published comparison explicitly leaves open.
decision_gaps: Does the free 30-day side-by-side comparison (E16) require booking an Enterprise-style demo as the proof-of-concept offer (E5) implies, or is it available self-serve to Free/Self-serve plan customers without a sales call?
Does Simple Analytics' own comparison documentation distinguish a consent-caused pageview gap from blocking or general implementation differences, which the Hebban case leaves mixed?
Can the 30-day side-by-side comparison run fully within the Free plan's 1-month data history and 5-website limit, or does meaningfully sizing the gap require a paid plan?
defining_need_fit.supported_core_workflow: An independent, consent-independent pageview count to measure and validate the size of the GA4 consent gap, run side-by-side with GA4.

unverified_requirement_basis.Whether the measured pageview gap can be: to measure and validate the size of the GA4 consent gap

defining_need_fit.caveat: The one quantified side-by-side result in evidence (E15, Hebban) attributes the gap to a mix of consent rejection, blocking and implementation differences rather than consent rejection alone, and the 30-day free comparison offer appears with slightly different conditions in two places (general setup help in E16 vs. an Enterprise proof-of-concept requiring a demo in E5).
defining_need_fit.why: The required no-cookie/no-consent counting mechanism and limited non-personal data scope are documented, the side-by-side comparison offer is documented, and one real customer case demonstrates the resulting pageview-count gap actually being measured in practice.

ranked_relevance.why: States the core mechanism — no cookies, trackers or consent required — that makes the pageview count independent of the consent banner driving GA4's shortfall.
The closest evidence to the defining need: a real customer ran Simple Analytics alongside GA4 and the resulting pageview gap was actually measured (431k more, 27%).
States the exact offer structure the defining need requires — running Simple Analytics alongside GA4 for 30 days, free, with setup help to compare the numbers.
Documents the specific, limited data fields collected (URL, referrer, UTM, time zone, device/browser), which is the mechanism basis for why the count can run without consent.
Describes the practical setup-assisted trial, including help with proxies and custom domains, needed to actually stand up a side-by-side comparison.
Documents the required non-personal-data/no-DPA capability named in the audience definition, reinforcing why the count can run without the consent gate GA4 sits behind.
A generic customer-logo trust claim with no detail on how any of those teams used the product; immaterial to proving or sizing a GA4 consent gap for a focused first campaign.
True regulatory background (GDPR/ePrivacy/UK GDPR/PECR compliance) but not itself the pageview-counting or comparison mechanism this first evaluation needs.

problem_fits.caveat: Simple Analytics can show and size a pageview discrepancy when run alongside GA4 (E15), but it does not add a gap view inside GA4 itself, and E15 attributes the discrepancy to a mix of consent rejection, blocking and implementation differences rather than consent alone, so 'closing' the gap is not addressed.
problem_fits.why: The required no-consent counting capability plus a real side-by-side case (Hebban) directly address seeing and sizing a GA4 undercount, which is the core of this problem.

segment_objections.objection: The sizeable gap Simple Analytics reports when run next to GA4 may not actually be a consent-rejection effect — the one published comparison itself says the difference 'can come from consent rejection, blocking or differences in implementation,' so a skeptical buyer may doubt the comparison isolates consent as the cause.
segment_objections.answer: Simple Analytics' own published case is transparent that the observed gap may include blocking and implementation differences alongside consent rejection, so the side-by-side run documents a real, quantified discrepancy without overclaiming it is purely a consent effect.

segment_objections.objection: A buyer running a non-trivial setup (proxy, custom domain) may worry that getting Simple Analytics correctly installed alongside GA4 for a fair comparison requires paid help or a sales process they weren't expecting.
segment_objections.answer: Both the general comparison offer and the proof-of-concept documentation state that Simple Analytics will help set it up and optimize it for proxies and custom domains as part of the free 30-day side-by-side run.
